main_text.p: portet omnibus iis, qui spatia in curriculo philosophico conficere feliciter satagunt. Satagentia enim in hoc cursu est frustra, nisi præcognitorum sax[?] præferatur: quum, teste philosopho, omnis disciplina sit è præcognitis, & veluti anticipatis. Denique hæc ipsa materia fructu est insignis, idq; quatuor modis. Principiò enim occurrunt, quæ modò dixi, principia, regulæ illæ veri & boni, quæ ostendunt discrimen turpis & honesti, quæ docent, quid facias, quid fugias,

——— quid fiet utile, quid non; quæ denique existunt basis disciplinarum, & quia disciplinarum, etiam universæ vitæ. Tolle mihi hæc talia principia, sive cognitionis illa sint, sive actionis, labascet protinus vita nostra, & quia labascet, ne vita quidem, sed ipsissima mors, id est, caligo & horror, erit. Tolle notitias illas primas, protinus Cyclopica ingenia, facient
Candida de nigris, & de candentibus atra, hoc est, cœlum terræ miscebunt; adeoque eveniet, quod Homerus de lignis male compositis cecinit, ut videamus
Πολλά τ᾽ ἀνύντα, καὶ πάντα, πάραντά τε δόγμα[?]τ᾽ ἐλθεῖν.

Has igitur vitæ nostræ magistras oportet nos paulo altius cum animis nostris repetere & reputare, si velimus illas nobis esse normas. Qualis enim, amabo, norma, quam non nōris? Nulla certè. Normâ vel circino Geodæta non uteretur, nisi utriusque naturam & utilitatem

page.notes: The word after "nisi præcognitorum" is printed as "fax", which is not a Latin word; it is probably "sit" with the long s misread, so it is marked [?]. The dash at the start of the last line is printed as a long rule and is copied as a dash. The page is cut off after this line. The Greek line is set in a smaller type with accents; the word after "δόγμα" is doubtful. "nōris" carries a mark over the o that may be a circumflex or macron. A small printed mark stands to the left of the catchword and was not read as text. The narrow strip of letters at the far right edge belongs to the neighbouring page and was left out.
